headline: Recommended that Parks and Rec clarify and make transparent its park fee waiver process.
summary: Discussed park fees and the waiver process with David Gill of Parks and Rec. Recommended a clearer, more accessible waiver process for discussion at the next RPAC meeting. Also discussed trash in public parks, with no formal action recorded on that topic.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the previous meeting.
Recommended that Parks and Rec clarify and make the park fee waiver process transparent and accessible.
Recommended learning more about park trash from residents who live near the parks.

Recommendation to learn more: from residents who live near work park.

Discussion with David Gill about Parks and Rec Fees  
David provided an overview of the annual process to set fees, both indoor and 
outdoor facilities.  
David had met with a constituent who had raised a concern about the fee process.  
Purpose of application and fee process is to ensure that space remains available for 
the public and that when members of the public want to reserve space, they can do 
that.  
Fees are based on residency, the vast majority of rentals are from non-profit 
organizations.  
Fees were reduced at the community center, and consideration was given to having 
free facilities, but ultimately decision was to have some fee.  Some worry that people 
would reserve and not use.  
8–10% of Revenue Park brings in is through fees.  Roughly 70K-90K annually.  
There is a process by which fees can be waived.  There are not a lot of requests for 
fee reductions.
The application does not articulate there is a waiver, but it is listed on the website.  
This change was recommended to the application. 
Dave clarified the requirement of liability insurance vs. signing the waiver.  
Fee schedule is differentiated by resident/non-resident.  But fees are the same for 
profit vs. non-profit.  
Committee Discussion on Park Fees  
Fees are consistent based on facility and amenities. 
Fees are in place to reserve space - which restricts access/availability for the public 
park.   
There’s an opportunity to increase transparency about the waiver.  
Fees to use city amenities are lower than other non-profits and organizations that 
offer space to the public (Women’s club, churches).  
Some discussion if the waiver fee actually could create some fairness/equity 
concerns.  
Sheila O’Leary Zakre, proposed a resolution “we would like to see a uniform waiver 
policy to be developed for a uniform policy that is applied uniformly”.  
Discussion of flexibility and clarity/transparently that’s applied consistently.  And 
amendment was made to include “other”.  
The spirit of the recommendation is to clarify and make accessible the waiver 
process.  
Recommendation on Park Fees :  
The committee recommends the parks and rec department clarifies and makes 
transparent and accessible the waiver process for discussion at the next RPAC 
meeting.   
Discussion with David Gill about Trash in Public Parks 
David gives a brief overview of how trash has been handled across parks.   
Reference photos/handout. (Note, there is a typo to the heading on the bottom of 
page 1.  Should say July 2025).  
RPAC decided to remove trash cans in July.  
This summer there is persistent trash challenges at Keech.  Sometimes this 
happens at White Park on the Weekend.  
Parks and Rec have updated signage in multiple languages.  
All groups are responsible for their own trash.  
It’s been dramatically different this summer from last summer.  
Dave’s recommendation is more work to be done to work with community leaders 
and members that are the biggest users of the park.  
Discussion of all parks becoming carry in and carry out.   
Discussion of a Park Equity Analysis (See Hand Out).  
Discussion of what has been put in place, signage and need to see those things play 
out a bit.  
Discussion of if the cities resources are distributed equally across parks, 
recommendation by a committee member to carry in carry out.   
Some potential solutions by making investments in technology enabled trash cans, 
although perhaps cost prohibitive at this time.  
Recommendation to learn more: from residents who live near work park.
